question: Hours of work to be considered full time?
text:
In the U.S., **40 hours a week is a common full-time schedule, but it’s not a legal minimum.** The Fair Labor Standards Act doesn’t define full-time employment, so employers generally set their own cutoff. ([dol.gov](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/flsa/faq?utm_source=openai))

For **health coverage under the Affordable Care Act’s employer rules**, full-time means averaging **at least 30 hours of service per week**, or **130 hours per month**. ([irs.gov](https://www.irs.gov/affordable-care-act/employers/identifying-full-time-employees?utm_source=openai))

If you’re asking about your own job, check your employee handbook or ask HR what cutoff applies to your job status and the specific benefit you’re asking about.
